Title: Fill every operator slot
Rule: A MathEquationBalancer instance supplies an ordered sequence of operands with question-mark operator slots.
A valid response fills every registered operator slot with an allowed operator.

Title: Preserve operand order
Rule: The supplied operands must remain in exactly their registered order.
Do not reorder, delete, duplicate, or replace an operand.

Title: Use the registered operator set
Rule: Each inserted operator must belong to the task's allowed set: addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division.
Do not introduce a different operation.

Title: Respect evaluation semantics
Rule: Evaluate the filled expression under the registered arithmetic semantics: multiplication and division have higher precedence than addition and subtraction, with left associativity within each precedence level.

Title: Return a complete filled equation
Rule: A scientifically valid response is a complete operator-filled equation matching the registered operand sequence and right-hand target.
The right-hand numeric target by itself is not a complete MathEquationBalancer response.

Title: Make the equation true
Rule: The filled left-hand expression must evaluate exactly to the registered right-hand target.
Every operator slot, operand, and target must satisfy the same equation.

Title: Bare target is insufficient
Rule: Returning only verifier_spec.target_value does not demonstrate an operator assignment and is invalid under the locked MathEquationBalancer task semantics.

Title: Alternative valid operator assignments
Rule: The frozen verifier_spec.target is the canonical construction solution used for deterministic worked examples.
Another complete operator assignment may also be correct if it preserves the registered operand order, uses only allowed operators, and makes the full equation exactly true.

Title: Precedence changes results
Rule: For a sequence containing both multiplication or division and addition or subtraction, evaluate multiplication and division first under the registered precedence rule.
Do not evaluate all operators strictly from left to right.

Title: Division by zero
Rule: An inserted division operator is invalid whenever its denominator evaluates to zero under the registered expression structure.

Title: Negative values
Rule: A negative intermediate value or negative registered target is not inherently invalid.
Correctness depends on the exact value of the complete filled equation.

Title: No unregistered parentheses
Rule: The current canonical MathEquationBalancer response grammar does not add parentheses that are absent from the registered operator-slot instance.
Solve the equation by filling the existing slots under the registered precedence law.

Title: Compare target scale
Rule: Use the magnitude and sign of the right-hand target to prioritize plausible operator patterns.
Large positive targets often justify checking multiplication early, while this remains only a search heuristic.

Title: Account for precedence before choosing signs
Rule: When a multiplication or division is present, compute its local effect before deciding whether surrounding addition or subtraction can reach the target.

Title: Search operator tuples systematically
Rule: Treat the missing operators as an ordered tuple and test candidate tuples systematically rather than changing operand order.

Title: Use subtraction for controlled adjustment
Rule: After identifying a large intermediate term, subtraction can provide a controlled adjustment toward the target.
Verify the complete expression under precedence rather than reasoning from the adjustment alone.

Title: Check division exactly
Rule: When testing division, use exact arithmetic and reject zero denominators.
Do not rely on rounded floating-point agreement with the target.

Title: Final structural audit
Rule: Before accepting a response, verify the operand sequence, every inserted operator, the right-hand target, and exact evaluation of the complete equation.

Problem: 8 ? 5 ? 8 ? 2 = 36
Correct response: 8 * 5 - 8 / 2 = 36
Check: The response preserves the operand order, fills every operator slot with an allowed operator, and the complete left-hand expression evaluates exactly to the registered right-hand target.

Problem: 9 ? 3 ? 3 ? 6 = 30
Correct response: 9 + 3 + 3 * 6 = 30
Check: The response preserves the operand order, fills every operator slot with an allowed operator, and the complete left-hand expression evaluates exactly to the registered right-hand target.

Problem: 3 ? 8 ? 3 ? 1 = 72
Correct response: 3 * 8 * 3 * 1 = 72
Check: The response preserves the operand order, fills every operator slot with an allowed operator, and the complete left-hand expression evaluates exactly to the registered right-hand target.

Problem: 1 ? 2 ? 4 ? 9 = -71
Correct response: 1 - 2 * 4 * 9 = -71
Check: The response preserves the operand order, fills every operator slot with an allowed operator, and the complete left-hand expression evaluates exactly to the registered right-hand target.

Problem: 8 ? 1 ? 9 ? 8 = 10
Correct response: 8 + 1 + 9 - 8 = 10
Check: The response preserves the operand order, fills every operator slot with an allowed operator, and the complete left-hand expression evaluates exactly to the registered right-hand target.

Problem: 5 ? 3 ? 5 ? 5 = 3
Correct response: 5 - 3 + 5 / 5 = 3
Check: The response preserves the operand order, fills every operator slot with an allowed operator, and the complete left-hand expression evaluates exactly to the registered right-hand target.
